competing_causes.text: A leak is possible because sustained P5 anomalies involve paired taps at neighboring stations across distinct failure domains. Reviewed comparisons show local pressure decreases while the P5 comparison station changes little. This supports investigating the accepted interval, but pressure patterns are not proof, and an unrecorded operating change remains possible.

The P2 operating record predicts a pressure increase, consistent in direction with the reviewed P2 comparison, rather than the localized P5 decreases. It supplies operating context, not an explanation established for P5. The supplied log has no verified P5 action but is incomplete; absence of an entry cannot exclude an operating cause or a coincident leak.

The revised P7 record identifies a possible shared conversion offset affecting A/B taps at P7-ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, not independent witnesses. The reviewed P7-ST1-A decrease versus little change at P7-ST2-A supports that explanation, without proving every listed tap faulty. This P7 context does not establish an instrumentation cause for P5, whose supporting taps have no reported missing data, spikes, drift or peer disagreement in the accepted health claims.
